name: עִירִי
gloss: of a city; or my city
summary: Iri is the last of the five sons of Bela son of Benjamin, heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men (1Ch 7:7). The name is עִיר with the ending ‑î, which makes either an adjective, “of a city, townsman”, or “my city”; scripture does not explain it, and the reading rests on the spelling. The Ir of 1Ch 7:12, in the same genealogy, may be the same man.

evidence.note: The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth וְעִירִי, “and Iri”, five heads of fathers' houses.
עִיר, Ir, father of Shuppim and Huppim.
The noun with a suffix: זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ, “the elders of his city”.

note: No verse explains the name. A derivation from עַיִר “young ass” or from עוּר “awake” cannot be ruled out from the spelling alone. The Septuagint spells it Ουρι.
